Stated Claim / Post Context:
Three of Boris Nemtsov’s convicted killers were likely secretly released early and now live a ‘quiet life’ in Chechnya, investigative outlet Proekt reports — Meduza

Three of the five men convicted of murdering politician Boris Nemtsov were released early and are living in Chechnya, the investigative outlet Proekt reported.

Actual Article Body:
Three of the five men convicted of murdering politician Boris Nemtsov were released early and are living in Chechnya, the investigative outlet Proekt reported.

They are Zaur Dadayev, who was convicted of carrying out the killing, and brothers Anzor and Shadid Gubashev. In 2017, they were sentenced to 20, 19, and 16 years in prison, respectively. A source told Proekt about their release, and the outlet found indirect corroboration in leaked government databases.

Dadayev, who would not have been eligible for parole until 2028, left prison in October 2024. His release may have been a gift to mark the birth of his child, Proekt reported; while in prison, Dadayev had married a woman who worked for Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov’s administration. Dadayev settled about 50 miles (80 kilometers) from Grozny, the Chechen capital, and paid off a bank debt of 1.2 million rubles.

Proekt reported that the Gubashev brothers also married after their release. They live in a residential neighborhood of Grozny and plan to build houses. All three were released on condition that they lead a “quiet life,” the source said.

Another member of the hit squad, Temirlan Eskerkhanov, was released in 2024 after enlisting in the Russian military. The fifth man convicted, Khamzat Bakhayev, was sentenced to 11 years and has since completed his term.

Proekt said those suspected of organizing and ordering Nemtsov’s murder have never been punished. That applies not only to powerful officials — Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov, State Duma lawmaker Adam Delimkhanov, and members of the Geremeyev family — but also to Ruslan Mukhudinov, a driver for Ruslan Geremeyev whom investigators officially identify as the person who ordered Nemtsov’s murder. Investigators officially identify Mukhudinov as the person who ordered Nemtsov’s murder. Mukhudinov, who has been wanted since 2015, has most likely also been living in Chechnya all this time, Proekt reported.

At Meduza, we are committed to transparency about our use of artificial intelligence in the newsroom. The story you’re reading was written by one of our living, breathing journalists and translated from Russian using an AI model configured to follow our strict editorial standards.
